look_here_first: Spring-fruiting prairie sedge with 2–4 distinct rounded spikes and large flat silvery-white winged perigynia.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: usually 2–4 distant ovoid to globose spikes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perigynia broad, flat and strongly winged

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mesic to moist prairie, roadside ditch and shore habitat

lookalikes.differences: The broad flat white-winged perigynia are the giveaway. None of the other Carex in B105 has that papery silvery winged look.
